manufacturer.olivetti.description: Italian company founded in Ivrea and first known for its typewriters. Its computer business combined in-house engineering, industrial design and several families of IBM-compatible systems.
family.olivetti-pcs.description: The PCS family comprised compact late-1980s and early-1990s computers ranging from the V30 to the 80386SX. BluMach presents them as one commercial family while keeping boards and revisions with different hardware separate.
product.olivetti-pcs86.summary: Compact V30 computer with integrated VGA and unusual PS/2-style peripherals.
product.olivetti-pcs86.history: The PCS 86 is a late XT-class design combining a NEC V30, integrated VGA, an XTA hard-disk interface and two PS/2-style peripheral connections. BluMach has validated Resident Diagnostics 1.09, MS-DOS boot, EMS and a 20 MB XTA disk.
product.olivetti-pcs286.summary: Twelve-megahertz 80286 model with integrated VGA and IDE storage.
product.olivetti-pcs286.history: The PCS 286 occupied the middle position in the PCS line. BIOS revisions 1.37 and 1.42 are preserved; BluMach has validated POST, Extended Setup, MS-DOS boot and Customer Test with a 40 MB IDE disk. The keyboard controller's original internal ROM and some board-logic registers remain functional approximations.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.summary: Bootable 1991 TI/OLIMCU16 board running at 12 MHz with authentic Olivetti BIOS 2.06; its exact commercial assignment remains unresolved.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.history: This board uses the TI TACT82300 family, Olivetti's OLIMCU16 ASIC, a PC87310 and integrated Paradise video. The 2021 research suggested that it may have served as a replacement board for failed PCS 286 systems or appeared in some PCS 286S machines. BIOS 2.06 offers 12/12, 12/6 and 6/6 MHz modes, so it does not establish that this was the board used by the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.warning: IDENTITY UNRESOLVED: BluMach reproduces and boots this TI/OLIMCU16 board with its authentic BIOS 2.06. POST, video, keyboard, functional RTC, 40 MB IDE and 1/2/4 MB are validated. The board photograph shows a separate battery and no identifiable Dallas module; EMS remains pending.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.summary: Documented commercial 16 MHz model, but not bootable in BluMach because no verified BIOS is currently available.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.history: A 1991 Olivetti brochure documents a zero-wait-state 16 MHz 80286, 1 MB standard RAM, up to 8 MB on the system board, 16 MB in the system and 40, 80 or 120 MB disks. It is preserved as a historical model separate from the 12 MHz TI/OLIMCU16 board; without its own BIOS, it is not possible to establish whether the two names ever shared a board revision.
product.olivetti-pcs286s16.warning: NOT BOOTABLE: no verified BIOS is available for the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S. BIOS 1.42 belongs to the ordinary PCS 286, while BIOS 2.06 belongs to the 12 MHz TI/OLIMCU16 board; neither should be presented as confirmed firmware for this model.
product.ta-dario286s.summary: Possible Triumph-Adler counterpart of the 16 MHz 286S, preserved as a research lead.
product.ta-dario286s.history: The existence and exact identity of the Dario 286S require confirmation from primary documentation or physical hardware. It is catalogued separately to avoid confusing it with the 12 MHz Dario 286/P35 or assuming Olivetti firmware equivalence.
product.ta-dario286s.warning: EMULATION UNAVAILABLE: no verified Dario 286S BIOS is preserved and its exact relationship to the 16 MHz PCS 286S remains unconfirmed.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.summary: Sixteen-megahertz 80386SX model with integrated Paradise VGA, IDE storage and an optional 80387SX coprocessor.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.history: The PCS 386SX brought a 16 MHz 80386SX to the family's compact format. BluMach now represents the photographed HT101SX, HT113 and GC102-PC chipset instead of the incorrect HT18 model, and has validated BIOS 1.14, Built-In Setup, MS-DOS boot, 1–8 MB memory configurations, a 100 MB IDE disk and the optional 80387SX. The machine is usable but remains partial until broader software, EMS and hardware-level compatibility are tested.
technical.ui.preparing: Technical documentation for this machine is still being prepared.
technical.ui.intro: This page separates documented hardware facts, behavior observed in original firmware, and the current fidelity of BluMach emulation.
technical.evidence.reverse_engineered: behavior recovered from BIOS code and testing
technical.evidence.implementation: current BluMach status; not necessarily a description of the original circuit
technical.evidence.observed: observed in preserved firmware and boot testing
technical.evidence.documented_and_modele: manufacturer manual compared with the BluMach implementation
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.cpu_bus: NEC V30 at 10 MHz with zero wait states, according to the official September 1990 Olivetti brochure; 16-bit data bus with the 8-bit ISA expansion of its XT-class architecture. John Elliott's SeaSIP notes report 8 MHz for his unit, but it has not been established whether that represents another revision. BluMach uses 10 MHz as the primary historical profile.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.memory_: 640 KB conventional memory. Paired SIMM expansion provides 0, 384 or 1920 KB of EMS. Four 16 KB windows occupy 80000h–8FFFFh.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.video: Integrated Paradise VGA. The system BIOS also contains its initialization code, so a separate VGA option ROM at C0000h is not required.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.rom_lay: Two interleaved EPROMs, CSAB05 (even bytes) and CSAB04 (odd bytes), form 64 KB at F0000h–FFFFFh. The set contains system BIOS, VGA, XTA and diagnostics.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.bios_re: Resident Diagnostics Rev. 1.09. The preserved set passes its checksum and reaches the reset vector at FFFF0h.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.bios_id: For compatibility, INT 15h/C0h identifies the system as IBM PS/2 Model 30, submodel 109. This is a firmware choice, not the computer's commercial identity.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.diagnos: Tests CPU, ROM, DMA, PIC, timer, base and expanded memory, clock/calendar, printer, communications, drives and keyboard. The observed screen is revision 1.09.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.io_intr: The following addresses cover PCS86-specific board logic in addition to the usual compatible blocks.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.board_c: 60h–6Fh: keyboard, PIT/speaker and proprietary logic. Port 65h: bit 0 XTA, bit 1 LPT, bit 2 VGA, bit 4 COM1 and bit 7 startup/test latch according to the analyzed BIOS code.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.keyboar: Port 60h receives keyboard scan codes and IRQ1. Ports 66h–6Ah implement the board's dual PS/2-style peripheral interface; observed IDs are AB83h for the keyboard and 00h for the mouse.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.rtc: E0h–EFh: MM58167 and associated NVRAM. Commands B0h–B7h manage access and status; BIOS stores date, time and checksum in its own format.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.floppy: Compatible controller at 3F0h–3F7h. The physical bank selects 360 KB, 720 KB, 1.2 MB or 1.44 MB per drive with active-low combinations.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.hard_di: XTA interface at 320h–323h, IRQ5 and DMA3. The historical 20 MB configuration is a Conner CP3026 (615 cylinders, 4 heads, 17 sectors).
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.serial_: COM1 at 3F8h on IRQ4; the real diagnostics report two communications channels, while BluMach currently models the confirmed port. LPT1 is at 378h–37Fh, including special 37Ah behavior used by resident tests.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.video_p: Compatible VGA registers at 3C0h–3DFh and A0000h–BFFFFh video memory. Integrated-video selection goes through board control and VGA enable logic.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.ems: Page registers at 8400h–8403h; each selects the page for one of four 16 KB windows at 80000h–8FFFFh.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.jumpers: Active-low port 100h: bits 0–1 drive 0 type; bits 2–3 drive 1 type; bit 7 indicates an XTA disk. Per-drive codes are 00=360 KB, 10=1.2 MB, 01=720 KB, 11=1.44 MB. Bits 4–6 are not exposed as user options because the analyzed BIOS does not consume them.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.key_loc: The key/keyboard-lock state is reflected in bit 2 of port 66h.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.gui_beh: Automatic mode derives jumpers from installed drives. Manual mode can reproduce an exact physical bank, including inconsistent settings, for research and preservation.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.verifie: BIOS and MS-DOS boot; CPU, ROM, DMA, PIC, timer, 640 KB base memory, clock/calendar, printer, keyboard and EMS diagnostics. FDISK has also been tested with a 20 MB XTA disk.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.limitat: Electrical timing of the dual keyboard/mouse interface and some video-arbitration details remain functional approximations. Mapping the reported second communications channel still needs physical evidence.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.source_: Olivetti PCS86 technical notes by John Elliott
CSAB04/CSAB05 EPROMs, Resident Diagnostics 1.09, Customer Test and execution observations made during recovery.
product.olivetti-pcs86.technical.brochur: PCS 86, Olivetti Office Italia product sheet dated September 1990, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.cpu_bu: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz; AT-class platform with optional 80287 coprocessor.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.memory: Documented 1 to 4 MB configurations; BIOS tests base and extended memory during POST.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.storag: Integrated IDE/ATA. Preserved configurations include the 20 MB Conner CP3022 and 40 MB CP346.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.chipse: G2 GC101A + GC102 set, later incorporated into the Headland family. BluMach uses 86Box's GC101/102/103 device plus Olivetti-specific IOC02 logic.
GC101 combines peripheral control, timing, arbitration and memory control; GC102 supplies address/data buffers and parity. The design supports up to 4 MB, matching the PCS 286 commercial limit.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.headla: The current model exposes 1ECh as EMS data, 1EDh as configuration index, 1EEh as EMS map index and 1EFh as configuration data. This is BluMach's functional interface and is not yet claimed as a complete physical decode of the motherboard.
GC101/GC102 Data Sheet, 55 pages, preserved inside BluMach
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.bios_r: Sets 1.37 (one archival file was labelled 1.34) and 1.42. The 16 MHz PCS 286 S variant remains separate and is not presented as identical hardware.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.setup: BIOS Extended Setup stores floppy, drive geometry/type, memory and board options in CMOS.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.diagno: The observed Customer Test validates DMA controllers, keyboard, clock/calendar, protected mode and CMOS, and reports floppy, fixed-disk and configuration errors.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.rom_la: 128 KB BIOS at E0000h–FFFFFh. Revision 1.42 comes from two 64 KB 27C512 EPROMs, LOW and HIGH, byte-interleaved. The older set identifies itself as 1.37 although its archival label said 1.34.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.memory: Test 6 writes RAM-REMAPPING at 60000h and requires it to be readable at 80000h. This exposed a 128 KB alias controlled by memory logic; BluMach reproduces it explicitly while the chipset control effect is completed.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.ioc02: Ports 68h, 6Ah and 6Ch. Phoenix 1.42 expects the first 6Ah read to publish 04h (subsystem ready). The device also resets on warm reset so stale values cannot cause I/O CONTROLLER ERROR 2.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.keyboa: Routine at F000:D192. It sends FFh to the keyboard, receives FAh as ACK and then waits for AAh as BAT result. Keyboard Error 4 means exactly that FAh arrived but BAT did not finish before timeout; this finding allowed the sequence to be fixed without fabricating keystrokes.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.cmos_b: Phoenix compares the BDA equipment word at 0040:0010 with CMOS 14h. For 80x25, one floppy and no coprocessor the base value is 0020h. CMOS 0Eh holds diagnostic state and 10h the floppy type; checksum covers 10h–2Dh and is stored at 2Eh/2Fh.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.video_: No valid 55 AAh option-ROM signature appears at C0000h. Historical halves named Video at E0000 and BIOS at F0000 are actually parts of system BIOS 1.37. Paradise/Olivetti initialization is integrated in the main ROM.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.verifi: BIOS 1.42, POST, Extended Setup, MS-DOS boot and Customer Test execution with a 40 MB IDE disk.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.limita: The complete physical I/O decode, exact effect of some GC101A registers and authentic internal M5L8042-243P ROM remain to be documented. A functional approximation is used where no dump or schematic is available.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.firmwa: BIOS 1.37 and 1.42, Resident Diagnostics, Customer Test and POST traces. Original EPROMs, normalized images and CMOS states are kept separately.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.progra: PAL16L8 2P04 and 3P01 are preserved as JEDEC. The documented physical controller is a Mitsubishi M5L8042-243P; its authentic internal ROM has not been recovered. 62410C62.BIN is not that ROM and is not loaded into the 8042.
product.olivetti-pcs286.technical.brochu: PCS 286, Olivetti Office Italia product sheet dated October 1989, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.cpu_b: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz; BIOS modes 12/12, 12/6 and 6/6 MHz; socket for an optional 80287 coprocessor.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.memor: 1, 2 and 4 MB are validated on the TI/OLIMCU16 board. Total 8 and 16 MB profiles also boot using a hypothetical generic ISA/AT card providing 4 or 12 MB from the 4 MB address. These profiles prove technical feasibility, not the existence of a specific Olivetti card.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.stora: The brochure offers one 1.44 MB floppy and 40, 80 or 120 MB hard disks. BIOS 2.06 has now been validated booting a 40 MB CP346 (805 cylinders, 4 heads, 26 sectors); 80 and 120 MB remain pending.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.bios_: Olivetti BIOS and Resident Diagnostics 2.06 dated 20 May 1991. Two 64 KiB EPROMs exactly reconstruct the 128 KiB FULL image; Setup supports English, Italian, German, French and Spanish.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.video: The integrated Paradise VGA is now initialized by BIOS 2.06 and renders Resident Diagnostics and Extended Setup correctly; no external video ROM is required.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.frequ: Extended Setup offers 12/12, 12/6 and 6/6 MHz, so BluMach catalogues and runs this board at 12 MHz. This supports the community hypothesis of a TI service board or shared revision without turning it into the commercial 16 MHz PCS 286S; F7 remains unmodeled.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.olimc: BIOS 2.06 probes 0208h, 0218h, 0258h, 0268h, 02A8h, 02B8h and 02E8h. It initially uses 0208h while sizing RAM, then relocates the interface to 0218h, with four 16 KB windows at base+0000h/+4000h/+8000h/+C000h. BluMach now reproduces this renegotiation and the observed aliases; the exact TACT82300/OLIMCU16 division remains unresolved.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.verif: Machine certified with documented limits: BIOS 2.06, POST, integrated Paradise VGA, RTC, keyboard—including the MS-DOS F3-reset-F2 sequence—40 MB CP346 boot and 1/2/4 MB board memory. Its identity is presented as a 12 MHz TI PCS 286/S; 8/16 MB totals use hypothetical ISA/AT expansion.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.limit: EMS remains pending: HIMEM.SYS can manage XMS on the 80286, but EMM386 cannot run on a 286 and no OLIMCU- or Olivetti-card-specific EMS driver is preserved. Shadow and F7/clock switching are still incomplete. The 8/16 MB ISA profiles do not reproduce an identified historical card.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.broch: PCS 286 S, Italian Olivetti brochure dated June 1991, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.board: 2021 preservation thread with high-resolution photographs and confirmation of multiple PCS 286 boards, including TI TACT82300 + OLIMCU16.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.credi: Thanks to the participants in the 2021 it.comp.retrocomputing thread, who documented the different boards and preserved the physical TI/OLIMCU16 evidence, and to EngiNerd89/Murdock for the Olivetti-PCS and Olivetti-OLIMCU branches, ROM names, inventory and port leads. BluMach later contributes disassembly, 0208h→0218h negotiation and 640+384 KB validation; it does not claim the original discoveries or materials.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.refer: Unfinished EngiNerd89/Murdock Olivetti-PCS branch identifying ROM 2.05/2.06, TACT8230x, OLIMCU16, PC87310 and Paradise VGA.
product.olivetti-pcs286s.technical.olimc: Historical Olivetti-OLIMCU branch, commit e1efcf6 (30 May 2021). It adds a provisional M290S using a NEAT substitute and explicitly records that OLIMCU16 EMS/shadow management is missing. Its comments note 0208h/0209h and 68h/6Ah, but it contains no OLIMCU implementation and is used only as a research lead.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.cpu_: Intel 80386SX at 16 MHz with a 16-bit external data bus; optional 80387SX remains pending physical confirmation.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.memo: 1 to 8 MB onboard; BIOS tests base and extended memory and stores configuration in 128-byte CMOS.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.vide: Integrated Paradise PVGA1A with 256 KB; OVC 1.06 video firmware is embedded in the known BIOS set.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.stor: Integrated IDE/ATA with documented 20, 40 and 100 MB configurations; the BluMach test machine uses 100 MB.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.chip: Confirmed physical population: Headland HT101SX + HT113 + GC102-PC three-chip set. BluMach models them as three separate devices and no longer reuses the HT18/HT21 core internally.

The exact HT101SX/HT113 data sheet has not been found. Board evidence and two independent BIOS families establish the 80386SX memory, shadow and EMS interface. BluMach assigns the firmware-visible memory controller to HT113, keeps HT101SX as the system-controller package and models GC102-PC as a transparent data buffer; this division is explicit and replaceable if primary documentation or hardware traces prove otherwise.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.head: Both the PCS 386SX Phoenix 1.14 BIOS and another surviving HT101SX BIOS program 1ECh–1EFh: EMS mapping data, configuration index, EMS mapping address and configuration data. Neither BIOS accesses fast A20 port 92h, so the dedicated chipset does not install it.
No public HT101SX/HT113 data sheet has been located; the older GC101/GC102 and later HT18 manuals are comparative references only, not proof of this chipset's register details.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.seri: TI TL16C451FN: one TL16C450-compatible UART plus a bidirectional Centronics printer interface. BluMach models that documented decomposition directly, replacing the unrelated PC87310 approximation.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.flop: Western Digital WD37C65CJM, represented by BluMach's AT-compatible uPD765 FDC core under the real component identity.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.setu: Built-In Set-Up covers date/time, floppy, disk, video and other board options. Its fields depend on the firmware's own CMOS format.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.diag: Customer Test exercises memory, clock, controllers and peripherals. U_MGR from the preserved copy hangs and remains under investigation to distinguish disk damage from an emulation incompatibility.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.rom_: Two 64 KB LOW/HIGH images are byte-interleaved into 128 KB at E0000h–FFFFFh. The global eight-bit checksum is zero. The first 24 KB contain OVC 1.06.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.kbc_: At F000:37C6 (physical F37C6h), Phoenix sends AEh to the 8042, waits for OBF at 64h and requires 3Bh from 60h. The generic 8042 only enabled the keyboard and left BIOS waiting; BluMach queues one machine-specific 3Bh response.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.ioc0: Selector is at 68h, data/status at 6Ah, with an additional 6Ch register. Phoenix 1.14 verifies 55h/AAh writes and expects 6Ah reads to apply XOR 20h; with selector 00h a write must not latch. Warm reset restores 04h/04h/FFh.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.memo: The provisional HT113 device exclusively owns conventional memory, 384 KB relocation, shadow RAM and EMS. With CR0 bit 2 clear, the 384 KB hidden by the upper-memory area is relocated above 1 MB. BIOS 1.14 does not contain the PCS 286 RAM-REMAPPING 6000h/8000h test; that copied alias and the generic AT remap were removed because they overlap the controller's maps.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.cmos: 128-byte Phoenix CMOS. BIOS 1.14 encodes 80x25 internal video as video bits 00h in CMOS 14h plus 20h in CMOS 1Ch; 80x25 external uses 20h in 14h plus 00h in 1Ch. The 80387SX updates bit 1 of 14h, and every change requires the 10h–2Dh checksum to be recalculated.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.vide: OVC 1.06 is embedded in the system BIOS and controls the integrated 256 KB PVGA1A; therefore the device does not mount an external Paradise ROM at C0000h.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.veri: Usable partial emulation: BIOS 1.14 POST and MS-DOS boot at 1, 2, 4 and 8 MB; Built-In Setup, internal PVGA1A/OVC 1.06 video, keyboard, CMOS/RTC, floppy, a 100 MB IDE disk and optional 80387SX diagnostics. The IOC02 self-test passes. An instrumented 8042 reset-entry probe confirms that CRI, MAR, CR0–CR4 and MR state survive a soft reset, while a hard reset recreates cold defaults.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.limi: Status: partial and bootable, not cycle-exact. No exact HT101SX/HT113 data sheet or original M5L8042 keyboard-controller ROM is public, so the register ownership and keyboard protocol are BIOS-derived functional models. GC102-PC parity/NMI wiring, physical HT113 warm-reset behaviour and EMS page mapping still need original hardware or diagnostics. General software compatibility has not yet been surveyed, and the preserved Customer Utility U_MGR module hangs; its disk history and DOS/Barrotes_1310 detection prevent treating that result as a confirmed emulator fault.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.firm: Phoenix BIOS 1.14, embedded OVC 1.06, disassembly of F000:37C6 and IOC02 paths, cold/warm boot traces and tests with/without an 80387SX.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.diag: Resident Diagnostics, Customer Utility 1.51 and Tutorial 2.2. Original IMDs preserve one unavailable sector; working RAW copies fill it with F6h. The sanitized Customer Utility copy remains separate from the original.
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.broc: PCS 386 SX, Olivetti product sheet dated September 1990, 2 pages
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.phys: Photographed PCS 386SX motherboard identifying HT101SX, HT113, GC102-PC, M5L8042, TL16C451FN and WD37C65CJM
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.tl16: Texas Instruments TL16C451/TL16C452 official data sheet (SLLS053C)
product.olivetti-pcs386sx.technical.ht10: Independent Emerson Elite SX386/16 preservation: photographed HT101SX/HT113/GC102 board and surviving BIOS using the same 1ECh–1EFh controller interface
manufacturer.triumph-adler.description: German office-machine and computer manufacturer whose Dario systems shared their engineering with Olivetti PCS models during the Olivetti ownership period.
manufacturer.triumph-adler.history: Founded in 1896, the company became Triumph-Adler and moved from typewriters and calculators into electronic computing. Its milestones include the TA 10 in 1971 and the Alphatronic family from 1979. Volkswagen sold its majority holding to Olivetti in 1986. TA subsequently manufactured closely related systems sold as Dario/P35/P45 and as Olivetti PCS machines. After restructuring in 1991, TA operated primarily as a sales company within Olivetti; it later changed ownership and has belonged to Kyocera since 2010.
family.triumph-adler-dario.description: The Dario desktop family preserves Triumph-Adler's branded versions of the compact Olivetti-era 80286 and 80386SX platforms. BluMach gives them independent machine identities while sharing verified board behavior with their PCS equivalents.
product.ta-dario286.summary: Documented 12 MHz 80286 desktop, equivalent to the Olivetti PCS 286
product.ta-dario286.history: Triumph-Adler marketed this TA-built platform as Dario 286 and P35 while the same motherboard was sold under the Olivetti PCS 286 name. The exceptionally detailed June 1990 technical training manual identifies the actual board assemblies, chip set, clocks, memory population, jumpers, CMOS layout and service diagnostics.
product.ta-dario286.technical.cpu_bus: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz with one wait state; Extended Setup F7 switches memory and I/O operation between 12 and 6 MHz. An Intel 80287 is optional.
product.ta-dario286.technical.chipset: The service manual identifies the G2 GC101A and GC102 controller pair plus the proprietary IOC. BluMach uses the GC10x core with the proven PCS 286 IOC02 behavior.
product.ta-dario286.technical.memory: CSAA03/06/09 board variants and SIMM combinations provide 512 KB, 640 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB or 4 MB. The standard 1 MB arrangement is 512 KB soldered plus two 256 KB SIMMs.
product.ta-dario286.technical.storage: WD37C65B floppy control and IDE disks. Documented factory drives include Conner CP3022/CP3024 20 MB and CP346/CP3044 40 MB models.
product.ta-dario286.technical.jumpers: A11 enables or disables the password; B07/B08 select DD or HD floppy operation; X04 selects the SIMM or system-board memory bank.
product.ta-dario286.technical.cmos: The DS1287 exposes 128 CMOS bytes. The manual documents floppy at 10h, disk at 12h/19h/1Ah, equipment at 14h, memory at 15h–18h and 30h–31h, language at 1Bh, video at 1Ch, password at 37h–3Fh and checksums at 2Eh/2Fh and 7Eh/7Fh.
product.ta-dario286.technical.diagnostic: Resident Diagnostics run at boot. Customer Test is supplied on CSFA12 and started with CUSTOMER; its floppy test writes to disk number 1.
product.ta-dario286.technical.identity: The Dario and PCS 286 are the same TA-built platform. In the absence of a separately labelled Dario dump, BluMach deliberately uses the preserved PCS 286 BIOS 1.37/1.42 set rather than inventing firmware differences.
product.ta-dario286.technical.verified: Shares the booted PCS 286 implementation: BIOS 1.42, Setup, Resident Diagnostics, MS-DOS, GC101/102 memory-control test and 20/40 MB IDE configurations.
product.ta-dario286.technical.limitation: The original keyboard-controller firmware is not preserved and is represented by the Olivetti-compatible KBC behavior. A Dario-labelled BIOS dump would still be valuable for archival comparison.
product.ta-dario286.document.technical: TA Dario 286 technical training manual DK000.00000.BA025, June 1990, 46 pages
product.ta-dario286.document.user: TA Dario 286 installation and operating manual (German)
product.ta-dario286.document.illustratio: Illustration supplement to the TA Dario 286 installation and operating manual
product.ta-dario286.document.components: Combined component data sheets referenced by the preserved Dario 286 board documentation
product.ta-dario286.document.wd90c00: Western Digital WD90C00 VGA controller data sheet
product.ta-dario286.document.tl16c451: Texas Instruments TL16C451 UART and parallel-port data sheet
product.ta-dario286.document.ld1107: Silicon Logic LD1107/VL16C451 UART and parallel-port data sheet
product.ta-dario386sx.summary: Triumph-Adler badge of the 16 MHz PCS 386SX platform, with preserved original ROMs
product.ta-dario386sx.history: Triumph-Adler sold the 80386SX member of this common platform as Dario 386SX or P45. Comparison of surviving version 1.14 ROMs proves that its executable video and system firmware is identical to the Olivetti PCS 386SX; only unused EPROM padding differs.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.identity: Offsets 00000h–05FFFh (OVC 1.06) and 10000h–1FFFFh (Phoenix 1.14) are byte-identical to PCS 386SX. All 40,959 differing bytes lie in unused 06000h–0FFFFh padding: mostly FFh on Dario and 00h on Olivetti.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.rom_layo: Original 64 KB LOW and HIGH dumps interleave exactly into the 128 KB FULL image. BluMach loads the Dario originals, preserving their FFh erased-area state rather than normalizing it to the Olivetti image.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.bios_rev: Phoenix system BIOS 1.14 dated 30 October 1991 with 24 KB OVC video BIOS 1.06, Resident Diagnostics and tables.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.chipset: Shares the PCS 386SX board model: Headland HT101SX + HT113 + GC102-PC, IOC02, discrete TL16C451FN serial/parallel and WD37C65CJM floppy control, plus integrated PVGA1A.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.verified: ROM reconstruction and executable identity are proven. The Dario uses the same corrected HT101SX + HT113 + GC102-PC implementation as the PCS 386SX and boots BIOS, Built-In Setup and MS-DOS with configured memory and IDE disks; its status is therefore the same usable partial level.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.limitati: Partial and bootable, with the same boundaries as the PCS 386SX: chipset ownership is reconstructed without exact HT101SX/HT113 documentation, the M5L8042 ROM is missing, EMS and GC102-PC parity need validation, and broad software compatibility has not yet been tested. Brand-specific external hardware differences beyond the proven firmware/padding distinction have not been independently validated.

manufacturer.trigem.description: South Korean computer manufacturer also known as Sambo Computer and TG Sambo, active under its own brands and as an international OEM.
manufacturer.trigem.history: Founded in Seoul in 1980 as TriGem Electronics Engineering, TriGem produced the SE-8001 in 1981 and became an important Korean PC maker and international OEM.
family.trigem-sx386.description: TriGem's own 80386SX OEM motherboard family. It is independent from Olivetti; each evidenced TriGem board and BIOS revision is kept distinct.
product.trigem-sx386m.summary: Independent TriGem 80386SX/16 OEM motherboard with Headland chipset, IDE and six ISA slots.
product.trigem-sx386m.history: TriGem manufactured this SX386M/KS-II board for OEM systems including the Emerson Elite SX386/16 and CMS Enhancements ESP SX386M. It is not an Olivetti model or rebrand. The Epson-hosted 20 MHz SX386M manual documents another TriGem revision.
product.trigem-sx386m.warning: EXPERIMENTAL: 4 MB POST, CMOS configuration and MS-DOS 6.22 boot are validated. All RAM populations, parity/NMI, low-speed mode and EMS still need validation; exact peripheral chips and the keyboard-controller ROM remain unknown.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.cpu_bus: Intel 80386SX at 16 MHz with documented 8 MHz low-speed mode; optional 80387SX.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.memory: Parity DRAM: 512/640 KB and 1/1.5/2/3/4/4.5/5/6/8 MB documented populations.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.chipset: Photographs identify Headland HT101SX, HT113 and GC102-PC. Sharing the reusable chipset model does not link this independent TriGem family to Olivetti.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.expansio: Four 16-bit and two 8-bit ISA slots; external video adapter.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.rom_layo: One 64 KB linear image at F0000h, expected as EESX386.BIN; metadata only, not redistributed.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.headland: BIOS tests HT113 at 1ECh–1EFh, clears 64 mapping registers and programs CR0–CR4 including CR2=DAh; no port 92h.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.jumpers: J2 enables 80387SX; JP4 selects LPT1/LPT2; JP6 selects mono/color; RAM follows documented SIMM populations.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.io: Integrated IDE, floppy, two serial, parallel and AT keyboard interfaces. BIOS-observed port 3F3h latch delays COM/LPT activation; exact controller ICs remain research items.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.video: Video is provided by an external ISA adapter; the motherboard has no integrated VGA or video firmware.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.verified: Authentic AMI firmware identifies Emerson, completes 4096 KB POST, detects COM1/COM2/LPT without false conflicts, and installs then boots MS-DOS 6.22 from a 40 MB type 17 IDE disk.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.limitati: Experimental. All RAM populations, parity/NMI, low-speed mode and EMS still need validation. Exact peripheral ICs are unidentified, so compatible AT approximations are used. Until master gains exact RAM-list support, the GUI also permits undocumented 128 KB intermediate values.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.manual: Micro House two-page CMS Enhancements ESP SX386M board reference; link and metadata only.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.vogons: Emerson Elite SX386/16 preservation thread with photographs, FCC identity, AMI BIOS and 80387SX jumper test.
product.trigem-sx386m.technical.epson_ca: Epson-hosted SX386M guide describes a different 20 MHz cached revision with up to 32 MB.
family.olivetti-m300.description: Olivetti M300 systems share a commercial family name but span several unrelated motherboard and chipset designs. BluMach keeps every proven platform separate.
family.olivetti-pcs-4xc.description: Early-1990s 486 members of the PCS range, catalogued below PCS while retaining their distinct boards and firmware.
product.olivetti-m300-if378.summary: Modular 16 MHz 386SX M300 with an IF378 CPU card and Intel 82335 memory control.
product.olivetti-m300-if378.history: The original modular M300 combines the IF378 CPU card, IN108 bus and GO477 multifunction board. It is not the same motherboard as later numbered M300 desktops.
product.olivetti-m300-if378.technical.ve: Resident Diagnostics and MS-DOS 3.30a boot have been observed with saved NVR state.
product.olivetti-m300-if378.technical.li: Bootable partial emulation: 82335 is modelled, while 82230/82231 and GO477 functions are composed from compatible AT devices; GO481 still requires external VGA. IDE and broader software need validation, and diagnostic wait-state helpers are functional approximations.
product.olivetti-m30002.summary: Early BA013/16 M300 with a 16 MHz 386SX, TOPCAT and integrated WD90C11.
product.olivetti-m30002.history: M300-02 is the 16 MHz professional BA013 product. It has its own firmware line and machine identity, separate from the faster M300-02F and the physically different PCS products.
product.olivetti-m30002.technical.verifi: The exact 128 KB R1.02 dump is identified, hashed and connected to a dedicated 16 MHz machine target sharing the BA013 core.
product.olivetti-m30002.technical.limita: Implemented but not yet boot-validated. The later R1.03 service BIOS is missing, and the TOPCAT and multifunction support remain partial functional models.
product.olivetti-m30002f.summary: Professional M300 with BA013/25, a 25 MHz 386SX, TOPCAT and integrated WD90C11.
product.olivetti-m30002f.history: M300-02F is the professional BA013/25-based product. It shares a technical platform with later PCS members while retaining its own commercial identity and product record.
product.olivetti-m30002f.technical.verif: Cold POST, firmware memory paths, EMS programming and boot have been observed with the recovered model.
product.olivetti-m30002f.technical.limit: Bootable partial emulation. Warm Ctrl+Alt+Del and an independent DOS EMM driver remain pending. TOPCAT is an initial register model; PC87310 and common IDE provisionally aggregate the real 87C310, Acer FDC and MSI logic.
product.olivetti-pcs11.summary: Compact A4-footprint system with a 16 MHz 386SX processor.
product.olivetti-pcs11.history: PCS 11 was a physically distinct home and small-business product rather than an M300-02F alias. It uses the BA013 platform with dedicated R2.04 and R2.07 firmware.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.verifie: Exact 128 KB PCS 11/16 dumps R2.04 and R2.07 are connected through a dedicated 16 MHz machine entry with a BIOS selector.
product.olivetti-pcs11.technical.limitat: Implemented but not yet boot-validated; enclosure-specific features are not modelled.
product.olivetti-pcs33.summary: 25 MHz 386SX office desktop in Olivetti's 1992 PCS range.
product.olivetti-pcs33.history: PCS 33 was marketed as a distinct office system with 2 MB and 40–120 MB IDE disks. Its preserved 6.03 firmware supports provisional reuse of BA013/25 without treating PCS 11, PCS 33 and M300-02F as aliases.
product.olivetti-pcs33.technical.verifie: The source-identified PCS 33 6.03 dump has its own 25 MHz machine identity and uses the recovered BA013/25 TOPCAT core.
product.olivetti-pcs33.technical.limitat: Independent product record. Exact board assignment and PCS 33 external differences still need a model-specific manual or physical inspection; the shared implementation remains provisional and partial.
product.olivetti-m30008.summary: 20 MHz 386SX desktop with OPTi 82C283, separate 82C206 and integrated OAK OTI-067 video.
product.olivetti-m30008.history: The BA319/BA324/BA325 M300-08 is a later compact platform, distinct from IF378 and TOPCAT. Its manual documents a 10 MHz AT bus and 2/4/8/10/14/16 MB memory; 6 and 12 MB are impossible.
product.olivetti-m30008.technical.verifi: POST, Setup, calendar rollover, 1.44 MB floppy access and MS-DOS 3.30a boot are validated.
product.olivetti-m30008.technical.limita: Bootable partial emulation. 82C283 is modelled and the AT bus is fixed at 10 MHz; common AT functions represent the 82C206. IDE needs a documented-disk test and RTC timing remains an approximation.
product.olivetti-m30015.summary: 25 MHz 386SX desktop with OPTi 82C283, separate 82C206 and integrated OAK OTI-067 video.
product.olivetti-m30015.history: BA320 was initially documented with an Intel 386SX at 25 MHz; AMD 80386SX-25 was a later board-compatible alternative. Its AT bus runs at 8.33 MHz and memory populations are 4/8/10/14/16 MB.
product.olivetti-m30015.technical.verifi: POST, Calendar PASS, floppy access and MS-DOS 3.30a boot are validated.
product.olivetti-m30015.technical.limita: Bootable partial emulation. 82C283 is modelled and the AT bus is fixed at 8.33 MHz; compatible devices represent the 82C206 and discrete controllers. IDE and a broad software set remain to be validated.
product.olivetti-m30030.summary: 25 MHz i486SX desktop with VLSI VL82C486 chipset and integrated WD90C31 video.
product.olivetti-m30030.history: The M300-30 is the SX variant of this 1992–1993 M300 platform. BluMach keeps it separate from the M300-30P although they share the board, firmware and peripheral support.
product.olivetti-m30030.technical.verifi: BIOS 1.09/Diagnostics 1.04 has completed POST, CPU, cache, memory, keyboard, RTC and protected-mode tests, booted MS-DOS 5.00 and retained the calendar. At 4 MB, memory is accounted as 640 KB base + 3072 KB extended + 384 KB dedicated = 4096 KB.
product.olivetti-m30030.technical.limita: Partial bootable emulation. VL82C486 is an initial model; WD90C31 uses the compatible WD90C30 core and PC87311/87312 is approximated by PC873xx. Other documented RAM populations and a wider software set still need validation.
product.olivetti-m30030.technical.manual: Olivetti service guide chapter 36; primary source for M300-30 and M300-30P.
product.olivetti-m30030p.summary: 50 MHz i486DX2 performance variant of the M300-30, using a 25 MHz external bus.
product.olivetti-m30030p.history: M300-30P retains the M300-30 platform, but its DX2/50 CPU warrants a separate machine identity and configuration.
product.olivetti-m30030p.technical.verif: BIOS 1.09/Diagnostics 2.00 completes resident diagnostics at 4 MB and reports 640 KB base + 3072 KB extended + 384 KB dedicated = 4096 KB.
product.olivetti-m30030p.technical.limit: Partial bootable emulation with the same chipset, video and Super I/O boundaries as M300-30. Diagnostics 2.00 labels the configured DX2/50 as DX2-66. Ctrl+Alt+Del can halt during early firmware initialisation, after the memory count or at a blinking cursor; use a hard reset for now. CPU timing identification, other RAM populations and a wider software set remain to be validated.
product.olivetti-m30030p.technical.manua: Olivetti service guide chapter 36; primary source for M300-30 and M300-30P.
product.olivetti-pcs46c.summary: 50 MHz i486DX2 PCS with ETEQ ET6000 and integrated Cirrus Logic GD5428 video.
product.olivetti-pcs46c.history: PCS 46/C uses board BA2036, based on the T.1 BA2044 assembly, with ET6000, 83C206Q, PC87310 and GD5428. M4-46 belongs to the related design family but is a distinct commercial model, not an alias.
product.olivetti-pcs46c.technical.rom_la: One 128 KB image: the lower half supplies OVC 1.09 at C0000h and the upper half supplies Resident Diagnostics/System BIOS 1.05 at F0000h.
product.olivetti-pcs46c.technical.verifi: POST, 4 MB detection, internal video, CMOS diagnostics, floppy/MS-DOS boot, a second NVR boot and Ctrl+Alt+Del have been observed.
product.olivetti-pcs46c.technical.limita: Bootable partial emulation: Setup date/time, IDE, the other RAM populations and broader software remain pending. Common AT functions currently stand in for 83C206Q; this is neither a dedicated nor cycle-exact model.
product.olivetti-pcs46c.technical.manual: Olivetti service guide chapter for M4-4x, M4-6x and PCS4xx (primary hardware source).
family.olivetti-prodest.description: Prodest was an Olivetti line aimed at accessible personal computing. The PC 1 combined a compact desktop format with a highly integrated NEC V40 design.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.summary: Compact 1987 NEC V40 computer with integrated V6355 video and a 720 KB floppy drive.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.history: Olivetti/Prodest International introduced the PC 1 in 1987 as the third computer in its consumer Prodest range, although it was an independent Italian x86 design unrelated to the earlier PC 128 and PC 128 S platforms. Built into the keyboard enclosure, it brought MS-DOS to home and educational buyers and reached Spain with a localized manual, keyboard and system disk. It was advertised at Informat 88 for 109,000 pesetas; contemporary reporting credited Mario Bellini with its design. Italy even had a dedicated PC 1 magazine.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.warning: PARTIAL EMULATION: BluMach now gives the V40 its own device and register model, using the compatible NEC V20 instruction core appropriate to its 8-bit external bus. Clock switching is implemented, but the integrated interrupt, timer and DMA units still rely on generic XT devices and a translation layer; the serial unit is only minimally modeled.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.c: NEC V40 with an 8-bit external bus and BIOS-controlled 4.77/8 MHz switching. BluMach uses its NEC V20 instruction engine plus a dedicated V40 system-register, relocation and clock-control device.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.m: The 1987 Italian specification lists 512 KB, expandable to 640 KB only through the expansion bus; the manual also documents a 256 KB base population. All three capacities are selectable and tested in BluMach.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.v: Internal Yamaha V6355D video with Italian character ROM 1.02 and a 50 Hz firmware default. The contemporary specification lists 80×25/40×25 text and 640×200×2, 320×200×4 and 160×200×16 graphics; BluMach models the Prodest-specific DDh/DEh interface and VRAM mirrors.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.m: Introduced in 1987 and sold from 1988 in Italy and other European markets. The Spanish edition is evidenced by its localized manual, keyboard and MS-DOS 3.20 disk; the base model was advertised at Informat 88 for 109,000 pesetas.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.c: The 1987 Italian reference configuration had 512 KB and one internal 3.5-inch/720 KB floppy; the manual also documents 256 KB, a second internal drive and expansion to 640 KB. PC 1 HD is a distinct 640 KB hard-disk variant, documented with 20 MB and implemented separately in BluMach as a partial emulation.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.a: Second MF 3510 floppy, external 5.25-inch/360 KB drive, MS 1040 mouse, JO 1040 joystick, monochrome and colour monitors, and a side expansion enclosure for two short cards. RAM, network, modem, EGA, CD-ROM, hard disk, TV/telematics and music expansions were also advertised.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.s: One or two internal 3.5-inch/720 KB drives and an optional external 5.25-inch/360 KB drive. The distinct 20 MB PC 1 HD now has its own initial partial XTA implementation and creation profile.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.i: Italian 73-key QWERTY keyboard with separate numeric pad and 10 function keys; partially RS-232-compatible serial, Centronics parallel, audio, analog RGB/SCART, digital RGB/mono, TV and DB-9 quadrature mouse/joystick. The side connector was marketed as IBM-compatible but omits signals of a complete ISA bus.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.p: The 1987 Italian specification gives 39 × 34 × 8 cm, 220 V/50 Hz mains input and 35 W power consumption.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.b: The 1987 Italian package lists MS-DOS 3.20, GW-BASIC 3.20 and Lode Runner.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.f: Known system BIOS revisions 1.06, 1.07 and 1.21 are 16 KB with valid checksums; character ROM 1.01 and Italian 1.02 are 8 KB. BluMach distributes none of these bytes and identifies them only by name, size and hash.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.v: With BIOS 1.07, 512 KB and internal V6355 video, the initial dedicated V40 model passes resident diagnostics and boots Spanish MS-DOS 3.20. The cold-boot prompt selects normal/4.77 MHz, and Ctrl+Alt+Del preserves either normal/4.77 MHz or turbo/8 MHz while passing the next interrupt diagnostic. The 256 and 640 KB configurations and a two-drive 720 KB installation have also been tested successfully through the unified creation form.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.l: The V40 interrupt, timer and DMA blocks are not yet native devices; generic XT functions and the existing floppy-DMA translation remain. The serial unit is a minimal register model. The quadrature mouse and incomplete external ISA-like connector are not modeled. GUI cold reset, systematic keyboard, serial, parallel and wider software compatibility still require validation.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.s: John Elliott's technical notes and firmware information for the Prodest PC 1.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.m: Installation and user manual for the Spanish edition (1987).
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.p: PC 1 Magazine, year I no. 1 (1987), page 23: contemporary Italian system specification.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.t: Italian community archive of PC 1 manuals, utilities and software.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1.technical.1: Independent historical catalogue entry for the machine.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1hd.summary: Distinct 640 KB Prodest model with NEC V40, integrated V6355 video and a factory 20 MB hard disk.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1hd.history: The PC 1 HD was sold as a separate member of the Prodest PC 1 family rather than merely as a user-selected disk option. Period Italian advertising documents the 20 MB configuration; surviving board photographs show BIOS 1.21 and a dedicated internal 40-pin disk connection.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1hd.warning: INITIAL PARTIAL EMULATION: BIOS 1.21, 640 KB, video, floppy and the factory 20 MB XTA path work; FDISK, FORMAT /S and autonomous hard-disk boot are validated. The controller reuses BluMach's common XTA engine and translates V40 DMAU channel 2 to a generic 8237 channel. The exact 40 MB selector geometry and native V40 peripherals remain unresolved.
product.olivetti-prodest-pc1hd.technical: NEC V40 with 8-bit external bus and BIOS-controlled 4.77/8 MHz operation; the current model uses the dedicated BluMach V40 register device over its V20 instruction core.
640 KB are visible to software. A technical guide documents 768 KB physically populated on the PC1HD board; the additional 128 KB are not mapped as conventional memory.
Integrated Yamaha V6355D with 16 KB physical VRAM mirrored at B0000h, B4000h, B8000h and BC000h. BluMach reproduces the aliases and their BIOS-controlled visibility.

One internal 720 KB floppy and an onboard 8-bit XTA controller at 0320h-0323h, IRQ 5, without an option ROM. The initial profile uses the BIOS 1.21 table geometry 667 cylinders, 2 heads and 32 sectors (20.84 MiB).
Dedicated 16 KB system BIOS 1.21, SHA-256 A2C03DC2E8752EA1632B910B4CE46AF7AB5FC6D4B352D8E21703B2ABB5791F96. ROM bytes are not distributed with BluMach.

A traced UCRT64 build passes Resident Diagnostics 1.21 for CPU, ROM, DMA, interrupts, timer and 640 KB RAM. With Spanish MS-DOS 3.20, FDISK creates the partition, FORMAT /S completes and the machine boots autonomously from the 20 MB disk. BIOS normal/4.77 MHz selection works and survives Ctrl+Alt+Del.

The XTA command engine is shared and the V40 DMAU path is an explicit translation layer, not a native integrated DMA implementation. Cold reset, PC1HD turbo-state preservation, sustained disk I/O, broader software and the documented 40 MB alternative still require validation.

family.olivetti-m28.description: Olivetti's first 80286 personal-computer family, centered on proprietary FE2000 logic and the indigenous OGC display controller. The M28's documented 1986 configurations combined 512 KB or 1 MB on-board memory with 5.25-inch storage.
product.olivetti-m28.summary: Eight-megahertz 80286 system with FE2000 logic, Olivetti OGC video and a documented 20 MB commercial configuration.
product.olivetti-m28.history: The 1986 M28 combined an 80286 at 8 MHz with Olivetti's FE2000 logic, 512 KB of standard memory, a 1.2 MB floppy drive and a 20 MB slim hard disk in the CPU 2801 configuration. Its indigenous display controller supported Olivetti monochrome and colour displays. Later expansion included 1 MB on-board memory and the ME903/MEM2852 memory board.
product.olivetti-m28.warning: PARTIAL EMULATION: POST, RTC, CMOS, floppy boot and 1 MB on-board memory are recorded as passing. The commercial 512 KB/20 MB profile uses a WD1003 MFM-compatible controller and ST-225 geometry as an explicit compatibility approximation; the actual Olivetti controller and drive identity remain to be verified. ME903 expansion, warm reset and two interactive diagnostics are pending.
product.olivetti-m28.creation.model: CPU 2801 commercial configuration: 512 KB, one 1.2 MB floppy drive and 20 MB hard disk
product.olivetti-m28.creation.hard_disk: Standard 20 MB Olivetti type 2 disk — WD1003/MFM-compatible approximation
product.olivetti-m28.creation.note: The profile represents the standard 20 MB Olivetti disk, type 2 in Setup. The blank MFM image uses 615/4/17 and the WD1003 controller only for compatibility; they neither identify the original Olivetti hardware nor replace the Setup CMOS setting.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at an 8 MHz bus, with Olivetti FE2000 proprietary system logic.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.memory: 512 KB was documented for CPU 2801 and can be expanded to 1 MB on-board. With 1 MB installed, the recorded diagnostics observe 640 KB conventional plus 384 KB remapped extended memory. The ME903/MEM2852 expansion board is documented but not modelled.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.video: Olivetti indigenous OGC controller, shared with related Olivetti systems. The current model exposes the aliases used by Customer Test, while an interactive alias retest remains pending.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.storage: The service manual documents a 20 MB slim or 40 MB full-height hard-disk unit and a controller at primary 1F0h, IRQ14 and DMA3. BluMach currently substitutes a generic WD1003 MFM path with 615/4/17 geometry for the 20 MB profile.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.firmware: Known 32 KiB BIOS pairs are PBUY/PBUX 2.09 and PBU6/PBU7 2.12. The 2.12 pair is the default because it is the latest locally validated set; the shipping BIOS for CPU 2801 is not yet established.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.verified: Recorded validation confirms cold POST, RTC/CMOS, floppy boot and 1 MB memory. The catalogue profile uses the documented 512 KB commercial baseline and launches without proprietary media.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.limitatio: ME903 memory expansion is absent. Warm reset, an interactive keyboard subtest and an interactive video-alias retest remain open. The hard-disk controller is a compatible WD1003 approximation, not a model of the original Olivetti board.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.service_m: Installation/operation and service manuals listed by the preservation source.
product.olivetti-m28.technical.brochure: Dutch commercial brochure documenting the M28/20 configuration.
family.olivetti-m250.description: Late-1980s Olivetti 80286 desktop family with integrated VGA-compatible Paradise video. M250 is the documented 8 MHz base model; M250 E is a separate 12 MHz board and firmware identity, not a speed setting.
product.olivetti-m250.summary: 1989 8 MHz 80286 desktop with integrated Paradise VGA-compatible video and 1 MB standard memory.
product.olivetti-m250.history: The April 1989 M250 brochure positions this 8 MHz, zero-wait-state 80286 as a lower-professional system. It specifies 1 MB memory, integrated 1.44 MB 3.5-inch floppy, 20/40 MB disks, optional 40 MB streaming tape, VGA-compatible graphics, three 8/16-bit XT/AT slots and integrated mouse/video.
product.olivetti-m250.warning: PARTIAL EMULATION: the preserved M250 cold-starts with local firmware and the 2026-09-03 test visually observed a software reset without Keyboard Error 6 in a newly-created NVR profile. Recheck with the historical NVR, visual POST/Setup/System Test and storage/RTC testing remain pending. The catalogue does not claim an original disk controller or geometry.
product.olivetti-m250.creation.model: Documented April 1989 baseline: 8 MHz 80286, 1 MB, integrated VGA-compatible video and 1.44 MB 3.5-inch floppy
product.olivetti-m250.creation.note: The manual identifies the on-board AT/RLL controller and drive geometries, but BluMach currently supplies a generic IDE compatibility path. No disk is generated until that controller and its jumpers are modelled.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.market: Lower-professional market, 1989. The manufacturer brochure names MS-DOS and MS OS/2 compatibility.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.commerci: The brochure documents 8 MHz, 1 MB, 3.5-inch floppy, VGA-compatible graphics and a 16-bit AT bus. The service guide identifies the on-board AT/RLL options: Conner CP3022 20 MB, CP3142 or CP346 40 MB, and CP3024 40 MB.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.physical: Manufacturer brochure: base unit 412 × 109 × 393 mm, 9 kg; keyboard 2 kg. It also lists 340 × 315 × 300 mm / 6 kg monochrome and 370 × 360 × 380 mm / 16 kg colour monitors.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at 8 MHz with zero wait states, as stated by the 1989 product brochure.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.memory: 1 MB is the brochure baseline and 2 MB is documented by the service material as the M250 limit. The catalogue offers both; only the 1 MB profile has the recorded isolated startup/reset observation.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.video: Integrated Paradise PVGA1A/OVC, presented commercially as VGA-compatible graphics. The local firmware set has a separate PERC 1.06 video image.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.storage: The on-board AT/RLL adapter occupies 1F0h-1F7h and IRQ14. Setup types are CP3022 20 MB (615/4/17), CP3142/CP346 40 MB (805/4/26), and CP3024 40 MB (635/4/17). P6 selects 40 MB 1:1 RLL for CP3142/CP346 or 20 MB 3:1 RLL/no HDD for CP3022.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.jumpers: P1/P2 choose the 512 KB, 1 MB or 2 MB on-board DRAM population; P6 selects the disk capacity/interleave; P8 connects the battery. These documented physical selections are not yet exposed or electrically modelled by BluMach.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.firmware: Observed local sets are PERB 1.03 system BIOS and PERC 1.06 PVGA1A video BIOS. Their bytes are local-only and are not included in BluMach.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.verified: Local isolated cold initialization at 8 MHz/1 MB; user-observed software reset without Keyboard Error 6 on 2026-09-03 with newly-created NVR. Historical records also report M250 POST, Setup and System Test boot.
product.olivetti-m250.technical.limitati: Repeat the warm reset with the pre-existing NVR and visually revalidate POST, Setup and System Test. RTC, OS installation, the on-board AT/RLL controller and its P6/P8 behaviour remain open. M250 E needs separate full validation.

product.olivetti-m250e.summary: Separate 12 MHz M250-family 80286 board with 82C206 logic and its own firmware identity.
product.olivetti-m250e.history: The M250 E is documented alongside the M250 in Olivetti service material, but has distinct 12 MHz timing, CHIPS 82C206 and GA80/GA99 board logic, as well as its own PDSF/PDSD firmware. Its Setup documents 20, 40 and 100 MB Conner types, while a standalone sales configuration and release date remain unrecovered.
product.olivetti-m250e.warning: EXPERIMENTAL: M250 E has its own system BIOS and board model, but complete visual POST, Setup and System Test validation is still pending. Its documented on-board AT/RLL controller and jumpers are not yet modelled; the generic IDE path is only a compatibility approximation.
product.olivetti-m250e.creation.model: Documented technical identity: 12 MHz 80286 M250 E board with 82C206 and separate PDSF/PDSD firmware
product.olivetti-m250e.creation.note: The service guide identifies the on-board AT/RLL controller and its Setup drive types, but BluMach currently uses generic IDE compatibility and does not model P6/P10 drive configuration. No disk is generated yet.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.market: Late-1980s M250-family derivative. Its standalone commercial positioning, release date and regional bundles remain pending.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.commerc: The service material documents the 12 MHz board, 2/4 MB memory populations and Setup types CP3022 20 MB, CP3142/CP346 40 MB, CP3044 40 MB (BIOS 1.07+) and CP3106 100 MB. No primary sales matrix has been located.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz, documented separately from M250's 8 MHz design.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.memory: Service material documents 2 MB using two 512 KB SIMMs and 4 MB using two 512 KB plus two 1 MB SIMMs. The 1 MB default is a current emulation profile, not a claimed sales configuration.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.chipset: CHIPS 82C206 peripheral controller with GA80/GA99 logic and an M250 E-only port at 6Bh. BluMach currently uses the shared AT peripheral path where 82C206-specific behavior is not documented.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.storage: The on-board AT/RLL adapter occupies 1F0h-1F7h and IRQ14. P6 selects 1:1 or 1:3 HDU interleave; P10 declares disk absent/present. BIOS 1.07 adds Setup type 7 for Conner CP3044 (635/4/33).
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.jumpers: P1/P2 select 1/2/4 MB RAM. P6 selects HDD interleave, P8 battery, P9 16 MHz versus 1.2 MB floppy mode, P10 disk presence, P11 serial port, P12 VGA and P15/P20 analogue timing. These are documented but currently unmodelled physical controls.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.firmwar: Observed local sets are PDSF 1.06 system BIOS and PDSD 1.06 PVGA1A video BIOS. They are distinct from M250 firmware and remain local-only.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.verifie: Local isolated cold initialization at 12 MHz/1 MB created NVR without a ROM-load error. It is not visual POST or diagnostic evidence.
product.olivetti-m250e.technical.limitat: Complete visual POST, Setup and System Test, warm reset, RTC, OS and all advertised memory populations remain pending. The 82C206 and the AT/RLL/P6/P10/P9 controls are documented hardware distinctions, not yet fully verified emulation distinctions.

family.olivetti-m380.description: Late-1980s 80386DX Olivetti desktop family based on BA806/BA818 proprietary logic. M380, compact M380 C and M380 C NEW are commercial variants of one documented platform.
product.olivetti-m380.summary: Sixteen-megahertz 80386DX desktop family with proprietary Olivetti logic, external controllers and local 1.09 firmware.
product.olivetti-m380.history: The M380 (BA806) and compact M380 C (BA818) share the documented 16 MHz 80386DX platform. M380 C NEW adds GO723 combined storage and GO470/481 VGA options; they must not be silently substituted by generic devices.
product.olivetti-m380.warning: PARTIAL EMULATION: POST, video, floppy boot and RTC initialization are recorded as passing. Proprietary CMOS/NVR checksum and warm reset remain pending. The current PVGA1A, floppy and AT services are compatibility approximations, not models of the Olivetti backplane, IF614, GO717/GO720 or GO723.
product.olivetti-m380.creation.model: M380 16 MHz 80386DX reference profile: 4 MB, external PVGA1A and one 1.44 MB 3.5-inch floppy drive
product.olivetti-m380.creation.note: M380 and M380 C share the selectable emulator platform. M380 C NEW is shown but disabled because its GO723 combined controller and GO470/481 VGA hardware are not modelled. No disk image is created.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.commerci: M380 is the BA806 desktop and M380 C the BA818 compact model. The documented M380 C NEW adds GO723 storage/floppy and GO470/481 VGA. This is an options matrix from the service guide, not a recovered price list.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.cpu: Intel 80386DX at 16 MHz with proprietary BA806/BA818 PAL logic; this is not the Headland PCS 386SX platform.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.memory: Memory is entirely on expansion boards: ME908/ME916/ME919 are 1 MB, ME912/ME927 4 MB and ME923 16 MB. Resident Diagnostics reports the 4 MB reference profile as 640 KB base plus 3072 KB extended (3712 KB): that arithmetic is expected, but BluMach currently substitutes linear RAM for the board/backplane logic.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.video: M380/M380 C use external EGA or monochrome adapters. M380 C NEW's GO470/481 VGA is documented but unavailable; the selectable PVGA1A is an explicit compatibility approximation.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.storage: M380/M380 C document external GO717 MFM or GO720 ESDI controllers. GO723 combined RLL/floppy belongs only to M380 C NEW and is not modelled.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.firmware: Local PBUQ/PBUZ 1.09 is a verified 64 KiB byte-interleaved pair. The service guide documents later 1.13 and 1.14 pairs, which are not locally preserved.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.verified: Recorded partial result: POST, video, floppy boot and RTC initialization with the local 1.09 firmware and the 4 MB/PVGA1A reference profile.
product.olivetti-m380.technical.limitati: Proprietary memory/backplane, IF614 floppy path, storage controllers, CMOS/NVR checksum and warm reset require validation or implementation. CAP7 documents LPT1 at 378h/IRQ7 and LPT2 at 278h/IRQ5; the current initializer omits them and Resident Diagnostics reports Internal Parallel Port Failure. The exact M380 Customer/System Test disk is also missing.

family.olivetti-m280.description: Late-1980s Olivetti 80286 desktop platform built around FE2000 proprietary logic, with external video and storage options.
product.olivetti-m280.summary: Experimental 12 MHz 80286 desktop with an 8 MHz bus, FE2000 logic, external OEC/PGC video, and locally preserved BIOS 2.16.
product.olivetti-m280.history: The M280 service guide records BA817 and BA824 system boards, an IF622 bus adapter, ME903 memory expansion, OEC/PGC monitor adapters, and GO714 MFM or GO723 RLL storage controllers. It is a service options record, not a recovered sales-price matrix.
product.olivetti-m280.warning: EXPERIMENTAL: the platform starts with local BIOS 2.16, but visual POST, video, keyboard, Setup persistence and boot are not yet confirmed. FE2000, the original console boards, OEC/PGC video and GO714/GO723 storage are not individually modelled; external PVGA1A is only a compatibility approximation.
product.olivetti-m280.creation.model: Documented base platform: 12 MHz 80286 / 8 MHz bus, 1 MB RAM, external display adapter and no asserted disk bundle
product.olivetti-m280.creation.memory.20: 2 MB total (ME903 relation is documented, but this total is unvalidated)
product.olivetti-m280.creation.memory.30: 3 MB (inferred 1 MB base plus the documented 2 MB ME903 maximum)
product.olivetti-m280.creation.note: The service guide identifies GO714 MFM and GO723 RLL controller options but does not recover a sales bundle, drive geometry or disk image. Creation therefore adds no hard disk. PVGA1A is an external compatibility video choice, not an Olivetti OEC/PGC model.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.commerci: The guide documents a 1 MB base system, ME903 memory expansion up to 2 MB, OEC EGA-compatible or PGC monitor adapters, and GO714 MFM or GO723 RLL controller options. It does not establish which combinations were commercial bundles or their prices; the 3 MB selectable total is an explicit inference.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz with an 8 MHz bus, 100 ns RAM access and one wait state.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.memory: The service guide lists 1 MB minimum RAM and ME903 expansion up to 2 MB. The selectable 3 MB total is inferred from those two documented facts and remains experimental, despite emulator support.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.video: OEC GO451/GO467 is EGA-compatible and PGC GO423 is a positive-monitor adapter. Neither original board is modelled; PVGA1A is used only as an external compatibility display for the creation profile.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.storage: GO714 is ST506/MFM and GO723 is ST506/RLL. BIOS 2.16 expands the hard-disk table and adds a 62 MB RLL disk option, but current BluMach creation does not claim a controller or disk geometry.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.jumpers: JU1 selects 512 KB or 1 MB RAM and serial/parallel enablement; JU2/JU6/JU7 select system and 80287 clocks; JU3 selects burn-in, monitor, and 32 MHz clock; JU8/JU9 control RTC/NVR clocks. Default positions are documented, but these physical controls are not modelled individually.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.firmware: Documented BIOS pairs are PBVW/PBVV 2.14 and PBVS/PBVT 2.16, with a 2.16.1 update. The local PBVT/PBVS 2.16 pair is preserved as local-only interleaved firmware.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.verified: Only build/runtime smoke testing and local BIOS loading are recorded. They are not visual evidence of POST, keyboard, Setup, video or boot.
product.olivetti-m280.technical.limitati: Visual POST, video, keyboard, Setup save and boot remain pending. FE2000, console, OEC/PGC, GO714/GO723, jumpers and the exact memory-board mapping require modelling or validation; generic AT services and PVGA1A are explicit compatibility approximations.
